note: The segments of the venue-sponsored journey that this repository owns. The venue-side segments — venue invited, venue pays, venue issues the invitation, venue reads its own metrics — live in the studio repository's copy of this manifest. Every segment here is either covered by named test files that `pnpm test` actually runs, or declared uncovered with a reason and an owner. There is no third state. A named file that exists but is not run by `pnpm test` fails this check: that is exactly the defect found on 2026-08-03, when seven test files across the two repositories were executed by nothing.

segments.what: A couple opens an invitation code and gets a sponsored workspace with the right access term.
segments.notCoveredHere: The mint-side guards, the wedding-date capture and the D-022 term arithmetic live in studio's entitlements-db and venue-lifecycle. See the studio manifest.

segments.what: One couple's workspace is unreachable from any other tenant, on every scoped read and write.
The four products the couple actually uses — Notes, Tasks, Timeline, Signal — enforce their own auth policy.
A published workspace is reachable only through the link the couple chose to create, and revocation is immediate.
segments.openRisk: R-031 and R-033 are undecided, not defects these tests can close. /p is deliberately search-indexable while the privacy documentation models every published surface as token-bound, and /embed renders a published workspace inside any third-party page. Both are product decisions that have not been taken. No test here should be read as clearing either.

segments.what: The only venue-directed read in this repository projects four aggregate numbers and can reach no couple content.
segments.openRisk: The route applies no D-011 suppression floor. That is not a disclosure today because its only consumer is the founder-only /hq/marketing roll-up, and the test pins that fact in place. It becomes R-027 on a new surface the moment a per-venue caller is added.

segments.what: A couple can take their content out and can have it erased.
segments.openRisk: R-023: account deletion destroys the shared workspace. D-027 point 1 schedules the fix before Cohort 1 is contacted. These tests cover the mechanism as built, not the product answer.

segments.what: The sponsored journey driven through a real browser, at real breakpoints, on a real device profile.

uncovered.reason: There is no end-to-end browser test of the sponsored journey. Playwright exists in this repository and runs under `pnpm experience:test`, but that suite covers the experience-quality fixtures, not the venue-to-couple path, and it is not part of `pnpm test`. Nothing anywhere drives redeem to plan to publish in a browser, and nothing tests a device profile or a throttled connection. Every segment above is proven at the module and query level only.
uncovered.owner: founder decision — see the E08.11 evidence document. Building this before the 2026-08-20 UI freeze is a scope call, not a gap an agent should close unasked.

segments.what: The unit a venue metric counts is the unit the definition names.

uncovered.reason: R-029, open: every adoption definition counts workspaces, but the attribution join runs on a subject id. One person with two workspaces and one workspace with two owners break the count in opposite directions, and the Tasks call site passes a different subject id from the other three products. A test written today would pin the wrong behaviour in place.
uncovered.owner: R-029, owner Claude Code, unresolved. E09.02 and E09.03 territory, not E08.11's to decide.
